annotations.text:
JR Importers — storefront redesign, three directions.

All three drop the current liquid-glass / floating-pill look entirely. Real catalogue data throughout (Samsung + Ulefone, live prices from the seed data). Device images are drawn placeholders — real product photography drops into those slots.

A · IMPORT DESK — editorial trade catalogue.
Paper ground, hairline rules, no radii, no shadows. Bricolage Grotesque + IBM Plex Mono; every number (price, SKU, stock, spec) is monospaced so the shop reads like the stock list it actually is.

Why: the pitch is "import prices, real shelf" — this looks like a supplier, not a marketing site, and scales to hundreds of SKUs.
Tradeoff: restrained. It sells trust and accuracy, not desire — flagship launches will feel undersold.

B · NIGHT COUNTER — dark showroom.
Near-black ground with a spotlight, Syne display, one lime accent, generous space, one product hero'd at a time.

Why: makes a N$26 000 handset feel like a N$26 000 handset, and the rugged Ulefone line photographs well against black.
Tradeoff: it lives or dies on photography — placeholder renders and phone-shot stock images will look worse here than anywhere else. Denser pages (catalogue, cart, account) need a lighter companion surface.

C · KIOSK — price-led poster commerce.
Archivo Black, 3px ink borders, hard offset shadows, lime blocks, oversized prices, sticker badges.

Why: price is the reason people buy from an importer, so price is the loudest thing on the page. Reads well on a cheap phone in bright light, which is most of the traffic.
Tradeoff: loud. Works against the premium Samsung end of the range, and heavy borders need real discipline on long forms — checkout, job cards, account.
